answer_text:
Let

\[
d=\min_{i\neq j}|x_i-x_j|.
\]

We will show \(d\le \sqrt2\), and then give a configuration achieving equality.

For two unit vectors \(x_i,x_j\in S^2\subset \mathbb R^3\),

\[
|x_i-x_j|^2
=|x_i|^2+|x_j|^2-2x_i\cdot x_j
=2-2x_i\cdot x_j.
\]

Thus

\[
|x_i-x_j|>\sqrt2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x_i\cdot x_j<0.
\]

So if \(d>\sqrt2\), then every pair of the six points has strictly negative dot product.

Now assume six points \(x_1,\dots,x_6\in S^2\) satisfy \(x_i\cdot x_j<0\) for all \(i\neq j\). Since six points in \(\mathbb R^3\) are affinely dependent, there exist coefficients \(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_6\), not all zero, such that

\[
\sum_{i=1}^6 \lambda_i=0,
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^6 \lambda_i x_i=0.
\]

Let

\[
I_+=\{i:\lambda_i>0\},
\qquad
I_-=\{i:\lambda_i<0\}.
\]

Both sets are nonempty because the \(\lambda_i\) sum to zero and not all are zero. From \(\sum \lambda_i x_i=0\),

\[
\sum_{i\in I_+}\lambda_i x_i
=
\sum_{j\in I_-}(-\lambda_j)x_j.
\]

Call the common vector \(v\). Then

\[
\|v\|^2
=
\left(\sum_{i\in I_+}\lambda_i x_i\right)\cdot
\left(\sum_{j\in I_-}(-\lambda_j)x_j\right)
=
\sum_{i\in I_+}\sum_{j\in I_-}
\lambda_i(-\lambda_j)(x_i\cdot x_j).
\]

Every coefficient \(\lambda_i(-\lambda_j)\) is positive, and every dot product \(x_i\cdot x_j\) is negative. Hence

\[
\|v\|^2<0,
\]

which is impossible. Therefore six points on \(S^2\) cannot have all pairwise distances strictly larger than \(\sqrt2\). Thus

\[
M_6\le \sqrt2.
\]

It remains to show that \(\sqrt2\) is attainable. Take the six vertices of a regular octahedron:

\[
\pm e_1,\ \pm e_2,\ \pm e_3,
\]

where \(e_1,e_2,e_3\) are the standard basis vectors in \(\mathbb R^3\). For any two distinct vertices, the dot product is either \(0\) or \(-1\). Hence their distances are either

\[
\sqrt{2-2\cdot 0}=\sqrt2
\]

or

\[
\sqrt{2-2(-1)}=2.
\]

So the minimum pairwise distance is \(\sqrt2\).

Therefore

\[
\boxed{M_6=\sqrt2}.
\]
